TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

notes.content: CONCENTRATIONS The B.A. in Music has 3 concentrations: General Music Studies, Music Industry Studies, and Music, Sound and Technology. MAJOR INFORMATION Any student accepted for admission to CSUSB can declare music as a major and pursue the BA in Music degree. Students may pursue any of three concentrations offered within the BA in Music degree: General Music Studies (GMS), Music Industry Studies (MIS), or Music, Sound, & Technology (MST). All new music majors should schedule an audition with department faculty in order to determine placement in applied music lessons and performance ensembles. Incoming students are also encouraged to take a keyboard skills proficiency diagnostic examination and a music theory diagnostic examination. Applied instruction is available only to declared music majors. Students interested in applied composition will be required to complete one year of applied vocal or instrumental music instruction as a prerequisite. Students in applied music technology or applied commercial music will be required to complete two years of applied vocal or instrumental music instruction as a prerequisite. Students may enroll in a maximum of four units at any one collegiate level of applied instruction. After four semesters at one level, students unable to satisfy completion requirements for that level will be counseled to select a major in a different discipline and will be denied enrollment in any higher level of applied instruction. All students enrolled as full-time music majors in the General Music Studies concentration are required to participate each semester until graduation (8 total) in a major performing ensemble most appropriate to a student's applied emphasis. Students enrolled in the Music Industry Studies and the Music, Sound, & Technology concentrations are required to participate for at least 4 semesters in a major performing ensemble. ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS The complete list of major requirements is available here: http://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/music/music-ba/ ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES **CLASS PIANO REQUIREMENT: The piano proficiency (class piano) requirement can also be met by successful completion of credit by examination administered by the department. **AREA OF STUDY: Students must complete four lower-division units in the SAME instrument/area of study. **ARTICULATES AS A SERIES ONLY: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible. ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) All concentrations in this major are similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Music. Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met. Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.

CONCENTRATIONS

The B.A. in Music has 3 concentrations: General Music Studies, Music Industry Studies, and Music, Sound and Technology.


MAJOR INFORMATION

Any student accepted for admission to CSUSB can declare music as a major and pursue the BA in Music degree. Students may pursue any of three concentrations offered within the BA in Music degree: General Music Studies (GMS), Music Industry Studies (MIS), or Music, Sound, & Technology (MST).


All new music majors should schedule an audition with department faculty in order to determine placement in applied music lessons and performance ensembles. Incoming students are also encouraged to take a keyboard skills proficiency diagnostic examination and a music theory diagnostic examination.


Applied instruction is available only to declared music majors. Students interested in applied composition will be required to complete one year of applied vocal or instrumental music instruction as a prerequisite. Students in applied music technology or applied commercial music will be required to complete two years of applied vocal or instrumental music instruction as a prerequisite. Students may enroll in a maximum of four units at any one collegiate level of applied instruction. After four semesters at one level, students unable to satisfy completion requirements for that level will be counseled to select a major in a different discipline and will be denied enrollment in any higher level of applied instruction.


All students enrolled as full-time music majors in the General Music Studies concentration are required to participate each semester until graduation (8 total) in a major performing ensemble most appropriate to a student's applied emphasis. Students enrolled in the Music Industry Studies and the Music, Sound, & Technology concentrations are required to participate for at least 4 semesters in a major performing ensemble.


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: http://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/music/music-ba/


ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES

**CLASS PIANO REQUIREMENT: The piano proficiency (class piano) requirement can also be met by successful completion of credit by examination administered by the department.

**AREA OF STUDY: Students must complete four lower-division units in the SAME instrument/area of study.

**ARTICULATES AS A SERIES ONLY: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible.


ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

All concentrations in this major are similar to the Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) in Music.


Completion of the ADT guarantees that students will be able to graduate from a similar-designated major at CSUSB in no more than 60 semester units. The ADT does not guarantee that all lower-division requirements are met.


Community college transfer students with a compatible ADT MUST meet with an academic advisor early in their first term and each subsequent term to stay on track for graduation.
